extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate mathematics instructors, mathematics education researchers, and curriculum developers (especially those teaching differential equations)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, implementing, and researching an inquiry-oriented undergraduate differential equations curriculum that emphasizes emergent modeling, student reinvention of ideas, and mixed-methods assessment. The rubric covers instructional design goals, task design features, theoretical grounding, teacher roles, tools, and research/evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inquiry-oriented approach (students investigate challenging problems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students investigate challenging problems; teacher investigates student thinking. A - Learn new mathematics by engaging in mathematical activity; B - Affect beliefs about themselves and about the nature of mathematics and the nature of school learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes student-driven investigation of problems and the teacher's role in probing student thinking. The approach aims both at conceptual learning and changes in student dispositions toward mathematics. (Slide text: 'Students investigate challenging problems' / 'Teacher investigates student thinking' / 'A - Learn new mathematics...' / 'B - Affect beliefs...')

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher investigative role
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher builds models of student thinking, learns new mathematics, and figures out what next question or task to pose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The teacher is expected to treat classroom interactions as data: construct models of student understanding, adapt instruction, and design follow-up tasks based on observed student ideas. (Slide text: 'A - Build models of student thinking' / 'B - Learn new mathematics' / 'C - Figure out what next question or task to pose')

rubrics_metrics.name: Design-based research principles for curriculum development
rubrics_metrics.description: Task design, ongoing analysis, guided by an instructional design theory and a theoretical framework for learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curriculum development should follow design-based research: iteratively design tasks, collect data and analyze, and ground decisions in both an instructional design theory and a learning theory. (Slide: 'Design Based Research (Cobb, 2000)' with listed elements.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use-inspired research orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Position research as use-inspired (Pasteur’s quadrant) — addressing practical educational use while contributing to fundamental understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames the project as balancing practical classroom improvement with theoretical contributions rather than purely applied or purely basic research. (Slide: Quadrant model of Scientific Research (Stokes, 1997))

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed-methods empirical investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic investigations of student learning should combine quantitative methods (statistical analysis, written pretests/post-tests) and qualitative methods (individual interviews, interpretative analysis, classroom interaction studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use written instruments to ascertain prevalence and effectiveness, and interviews and classroom analyses to probe mechanisms and provide interpretive detail. (Slide text lists methods and purposes.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical grounding: dynamical systems + Realistic Mathematics Education
rubrics_metrics.description: Curriculum should be grounded in a dynamical systems point of view and the instructional design theory of Realistic Mathematics Education (RME).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design should support co-emergent analytic, numerical, and graphical approaches, systematic study of student thinking, and modeling. The RME emergent model heuristic guides task sequencing from situational to formal activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-emergent analytic, numerical, and graphical approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach analytic, numerical, and graphical methods so they emerge together rather than treating analytic methods as primary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage students to develop algebraic techniques from empirical/graphical exploration; do not isolate analytic techniques from modeling and visualization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of innovative technological tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate technological tools (e.g., Java applets) to allow empirical exploration of vector fields, parameter variation, and solution behaviors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technology supports exploration tasks (e.g., varying friction coefficient) and helps students form conjectures that drive mathematization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative pedagogy: social negotiation of meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Foster social negotiation of meaning in the classroom; use student discussion and group work as core pedagogical mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group presentations and class discussion are used both to surface student thinking and as a basis for introducing formal terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student reinvention of mathematical ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Design activities so that students (with guidance) reinvent many key mathematical ideas rather than being presented formalism first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges reinvention takes more time; tasks should scaffold empirical discovery leading to algebraic generalization (e.g., reinvention of eigensolutions and bifurcation diagrams).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended learning outcomes: conceptual depth, retention, and dispositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether students learn ideas more deeply, retain knowledge longer, and develop more productive dispositions about mathematics and their ability to do mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment plans should include measures for conceptual understanding, delayed retention, and attitude/disposition shifts (student testimonies and attitude measures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment dimensions: routine vs conceptual vs modeling/graphical
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess student learning across categories such as routine/procedural tasks and conceptual/modeling/graphical tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pre/post and delayed post-tests with items categorized (e.g., Routine, Conceptual, QG (Qualitatively/Graphically), M (Modeling), PO (Procedurally Oriented)) and report comparative results across instructional conditions (IODE vs traditional).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional sequence: Prediction → Exploration → Mathematization → Generalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a sequence where students first predict, then explore empirically (often with technology), then mathematize their observations (invent algebraic descriptions), and finally generalize to broader situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The flow supports reinvention: prediction elicits initial ideas; exploration creates cognitive disequilibrium and data; mathematization codifies patterns; generalization abstracts the methods to other problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergent Model Heuristic stages (RME): situational, referential, general, formal activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Tasks should move learners through: situational activity (experiential setting), referential activity (models that refer to the situation), general activity (models-for independent of original context), and formal activity (mathematical reasoning not requiring original context).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design tasks and teacher moves so that students progress from context-specific modeling to formal mathematical representations and reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task design features: prediction tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Prediction tasks ask students to anticipate behavior (e.g., draw position-velocity graphs) to surface preconceptions and create motivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prediction prompts to generate diverse student hypotheses that can be empirically tested during exploration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task design features: exploration tasks with parameter variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploration tasks let students empirically change parameters (e.g., friction coefficient) and observe changes in vector fields and solution behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploration with technology reveals non-obvious behaviors (spiraling vs non-spiraling) and motivates algebraic investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task design features: mathematization tasks (student-invented algebraic methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematization tasks require students to invent algebraic approaches that model their empirical observations (e.g., find slopes of straight-line solutions, derive equations for solution curves).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage students to use prior knowledge (e.g., y=mx) and rate-of-change ratios to derive quadratic equations for slopes and to generalize to complex cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task design constraints to focus student work
rubrics_metrics.description: Design constraints (for example: do not ask students to find the best harvesting rate; limit reports to one page) to focus attention on reasoning rather than optimization or lengthy exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limiting scope and deliverable size forces students to prioritize key modeling reasoning and explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use student work as basis for introducing conventional terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructor leverages student-generated artifacts and presentations to introduce and connect to formal mathematical terminology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After students construct models/diagrams, the teacher formalizes vocabulary and links student reasoning to canonical concepts (e.g., bifurcation, equilibrium, phase lines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence instruction opposite to typical textbook ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor having students produce empirical curves or bifurcation diagrams first, then use those products to derive or motivate formal definitions and phase-line analyses (reverse of typical text-first approach).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sequencing supports conceptual coherence for learners: empirical creation of a curve is used as the starting point and phase lines/definitions add subsequent meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphical reasoning tools as central reasoning devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach students to use graphs (e.g., SLS graphs, plots of e^{rt} components) and ratios like y(t)/x(t) as tools for reasoning about long-term behavior and dependence on initial conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit attention to how component exponentials and slopes inform global solution behavior; use limits to reason about asymptotes and slope behavior as t→±∞.
